title.narrative: Activity under preparation Support to the return, repatriation and reintegration of Iraqis from North-East Syria

description.narrative: While efforts of return and reintegration of Iraqis from the camps in NorthEast Syria (NES) has been ongoing for sometime, following the fall of the Assad regime in Syria, the Iraqi officials have stated their intention to accelerate repatriation of all its citizens in 2025. The reintegration process, however, is complex, lengthy and challenging. Returnees face significant challenges, including stigmatisation, community resistance, and economic marginalisation. The absence of livelihood and employment opportunities further perpetuate cycles of dependency, while unresolved trauma¿especially among vulnerable groups such as women and children¿remains a significant barrier to reintegration. Building on long stranding the EU presence in Iraq and expanding the on-going support to the repatriation and reintegration of Iraqi nationals, this 18- month exceptional assistance measure aims to enhance security and stability through sustainable reintegration of Iraqi nationals returning from camps in NES, and strengthen the Iraqi government capacity in its efforts for the return, repatriation and reintegration of its citizens. The action will target Al Amal camp in Iraq, which is dedicated for returnees from Syria, those released for reintegration with a focus on four priority Governorates: Anbar, Ninewa, Salah al-Din and Kirkuk, taking into account the receiving communities in line with the government¿s reintegration strategy.
